*.text: Iowa's two big utilities, MidAmerican Energy and Interstate Power and Light (the Alliant Energy utility in Iowa), file Resource Evaluation Studies with the Iowa Utilities Commission instead of integrated resource plans. New plants need a generating certificate from the commission, and the filings are on the commission's electronic filing system at efs.iowa.gov. Air construction permits come from the Iowa Department of Natural Resources. Interstate Power and Light owns the Alliant plants in Iowa, so the immediate owner is Interstate Power and Light Co and Alliant Energy Corp is the parent.

L100001062091.text: A comment left in the database in February 2026 links a WVIK news story of February 12, 2026 headlined 'Controversial new power plant rejected for rural Scott County'. Find out who rejected Hickory Grove (the county board, zoning, or the utilities commission), whether Central Iowa Power Cooperative appealed or moved the project to another site, and what has happened since. The cooperative's project page still targets late 2029. A rejection alone is not a cancellation: record it in Status Detail with its link and change the status only if the cooperative dropped the project or a second publisher reports it cancelled or shelved. The unit still has no start year; give one only if the cooperative states a target year.

L100001062089.text: Owner(s) says Alliant Energy Corp, while every other Alliant plant in Iowa lists the immediate owner Interstate Power and Light Co. Check the generating certificate filing or Alliant's project page for the company that owns Cedar River Generating Station, and report Owner(s) with that document. Run the entity lookup before naming a company. The plant sits inside the Prairie Creek site in Cedar Rapids, and its coordinates are copied from Prairie Creek; give exact coordinates only if a document places the new plant.

L100001063341.text: Alliant said in October 2025 that it was deprioritizing the Fairfax site for its proposed gas plant, and in 2026 proposed the Morgan Valley Energy Center at a new site about 2.5 miles northwest of Fairfax (docket GCU-2026-0002, filed April 29, 2026). GEM already has Morgan Valley as its own plant. Confirm that the Fairfax site was dropped, with its year and document; 'deprioritized' alone may not be a cancellation. Then say in a question whether Fairfax and Morgan Valley are the same project, so a reviewer can decide whether to keep both entries. The Fairfax units have no owner: if a source names the owner of the dropped project, report it.

L100001081945.text: This placeholder holds the 430 megawatt combined cycle unit in Interstate Power and Light's 2024 Resource Evaluation Study, due in 2029. Check whether that unit has since been named and sited, for example as the Morgan Valley Energy Center or the cancelled Fairfax project. If it has, say so in a question naming the project, so the reviewer can merge the entries. If the newest Interstate Power and Light filing drops the combined cycle unit, say so with the filing.
